title: Minkä maalaisia: asking about several people's nationalities
summary: For several people, use minkä maalaisia and a plural olla form: Minkä maalaisia te olette? Minkä maalaisia te olette? — Olemme suomalaisia.
targetSkills: Minkä maalaisia: asking about several people's nationalities
prerequisiteSkills: Minkä maalainen: asking about one person's nationality
objectives: Ask several people's nationalities with minkä maalaisia.
Use a plural nationality description and the correct group perspective.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
The genitive is a relationship form; in these question phrases minkä means of what or which.
For several people, use minkä maalaisia and a plural olla form: Minkä maalaisia te olette? (“What nationality are you?” addressed to a group). Minkä itself does not change.
keyPoints: Keep the nationality question's descriptive word plural when asking about several people.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: An ordinary plural description uses the plural partitive nationality form: Me olemme suomalaisia (“We are Finnish”). In the taught -lainen words, -lainen becomes -laisia: suomalainen → suomalaisia. A group addressed as te replies with me or omits it with olemme. Keep he when both speakers refer to the same other group.
A natural short reply to “Minkä maalaisia te olette?” is “Suomalaisia.” (“Finnish.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
The complete phrase emme ole rejects the suggested nationality of the group. Both descriptive nationality words keep their plural partitive forms.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Use the plural descriptive nationality form for these groups.

paragraphs: suomalaisia means Finnish here. Suomalainen changes -nen to -sia: suomalaisia describes the members of the group.
ruotsalaisia means Swedish here. Ruotsalainen changes -nen to -sia: ruotsalaisia.
virolaisia means Estonian here. Virolainen changes -nen to -sia: virolaisia.
saksalaisia means German here. Saksalainen changes -nen to -sia: saksalaisia.

examples.english: We are not Finnish. We are Estonian.
steps: Emme: we do not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). Emme is the plural first-person negative verb.
ole: be; main verb after the negative verb. After a present-tense negative verb, olla takes the unchanged form ole.
